title: Stack vs Heap
concept: Stack is automatic but narrow, heap is manual but wide

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Include `#include <stdio.h>` for use with `printf`.

This lesson compares the differences in roles between the stack and the heap.

steps.title: Include stdlib.h header
steps.explanation:
Include `#include <stdlib.h>` for `malloc`/`free` use.

Heap memory is managed directly by functions in this header.

steps.title: main function definition
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Now compare stack array and heap allocation in the same code.

steps.title: Declare array on stack
steps.explanation:
An array of integers is created on the stack.

Stack memory is fast and automatically freed, but has small size limits.

steps.title: Allocating memory on the heap (malloc)
steps.explanation:
With `malloc` we request a large piece of contiguous memory from the heap and store its starting address in a pointer.

The actual data is in the heap, and only a pointer containing the address remains on the stack.

steps.title: Check heap allocation success
steps.explanation:
Check whether allocation was successful with `heapArr != NULL`.

Dereferencing in case of failure is dangerous, so confirmation before use is essential.

steps.title: Print success message
steps.explanation: Outputs the heap allocation success status.

steps.title: Free heap memory
steps.explanation:
Free the heap memory with `free(heapArr)`.

Dynamic allocations must be managed in pairs until freed.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: Stack is automatic, heap is manually managed.

quiz.question: In which of the following situations should the Heap area be used?
options: Temporary variable that can disappear when the function ends
When you need to create an array as large (dynamically) as the size entered by the user.
When you need the fastest speed
quiz.explanation: When the array size is not determined at compile time (dynamic) or when dealing with very large data, the heap must be used.

misconceptions.why: This is because the Stack is a simple structure directly managed by the CPU, but the Heap requires a complex algorithm to search for empty space.

keyTakeaway: A small and fast thing is a stack, a big and long-lasting thing is a heap.
